audit.whatIsWrong: The entry repeatedly assigns Volibear's stun to E and his slow to W: "Land E hand-of-the-god stun", "Unstoppable Force ignores his E stun cast time and W slow", "his W bite slows and heals him", "knock him up mid-E-stun".
audit.why: It is exactly backwards. Q Thundering Smash is the stun ("gains speed towards enemies, Stunning and damaging the first one he Attacks"); E Sky Splitter is the ranged slow that also shields him if he stands in his own blast. W Frenzied Maul does not slow at all — it marks, applies on-hit, and heals only on the second cast into the same mark. A Malphite told to dodge an E stun will stand in the one ability he can safely walk out of and eat the one he cannot.
audit.corrected: Q Thundering Smash named as the stun, E Sky Splitter as the slow-and-shield, W Frenzied Maul as the 5s double-cast heal. Applied across spikes[0], spikes[1], wants.foe[1], wants.you[2], early and whys.
sources: champ-data/_kits/volibear.json (Q "Stunning and damaging the first one he Attacks"; E "Slowing enemies while granting Volibear a Shield"; W "marking them... deals bonus damage and Heals")

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] calls Stormbringer a "tower-shield + global pressure" tool, and nothing anywhere gives an ultimate cooldown.
audit.why: Stormbringer is 550 range — the opposite of global — and it grants bonus Health, not a shield. The number that actually matters is the cooldown: 160/135/110 against Unstoppable Force's 130/115/100. Malphite has his ultimate back thirty seconds earlier at rank 1 and ten seconds earlier at rank 3, which is the concrete reason the level-6 and first-item stages belong to him rather than a vague "he's a scaler".
audit.corrected: Stated the 160s vs 130s gap in spikes[1] and whys[4]; removed "global" and "tower-shield" from spikes[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart hands Volibear five of seven stages including Level 6 and First item, while Malphite wins 53.17% over 709 games — and the entry's own spikes[1] and spikes[2] call those exact two stages Malphite's flip point.
audit.why: The chart contradicts the rest of the page. spikes[1] says level 6 "flips the lane" and spikes[2] says the first armour item "turns his auto-bite brawl into a losing trade for him", yet the chart labels both Volibear. Volibear genuinely owns levels 1-5 — Thundering Smash plus a 5-second Frenzied Maul against a Malphite with no Thunderclap — but the ultimate gap and the armour spike are Malphite's.
audit.corrected: Level 6 and First item flipped to Malphite; levels 2-5 left with Volibear.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown is given for anything in either kit, so "don't trade into his heal" has no timer attached.
audit.why: Frenzied Maul is a flat 5 seconds at every rank, so it is effectively always up and is not a window you wait out. Sky Splitter is 16 seconds flat and Thundering Smash 12 down to 10 — those are the two you actually count. That reframes the advice: you cannot dodge the heal, you punish the 16-second gap after Sky Splitter.
audit.corrected: 5s / 16s / 12s cooldowns worked into spikes[0], whys[1], whys[3] and mid.
sources: champ-data/_kits/volibear.json (W cd 5, E cd 16, Q cd 12/11.5/11/10.5/10)

audit.whatIsWrong: late says "your armor stacking and E attack-speed slow hard-counter his auto-heavy, AD brawl".
audit.why: Half right. Volibear's passive The Relentless Storm converts his attack speed into bonus MAGIC damage to nearby enemies, so pure armour does not answer the back half of his damage — and the attack-speed slow is doing double duty, because it cuts both his auto DPS and the passive that rides on it. Worth stating plainly rather than selling armour as a complete answer.
audit.corrected: late now names The Relentless Storm and points Ground Slam's attack-speed slow at it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/volibear.json (P "grant Attack Speed, and eventually cause his Attacks to deal bonus magic damage to nearby enemies")

edits.before: Volibear owns these first few levels — his empowered Q dash closes on you and his W bite slows and heals him through anything you throw, and you have no trade pattern yet beyond a Q poke. Don't try to brawl: last-hit at range, keep Granite Shield intact by stepping out after he commits, and respect that his sustain undoes your chip. The one thing to dodge is committing to a Q-Q trade when his W is up — that's a free heal for him. Just farm and bleed the lane toward your spike.
edits.after: Volibear owns these first few levels — Thundering Smash closes and stuns off his next auto, and Frenzied Maul heals him on the second cast into the same mark, every 5 seconds. You have no trade pattern yet beyond a Q poke. Don't brawl: last-hit at range, and step out after he commits so Granite Shield recharges. Frenzied Maul is never on cooldown, so there is no heal window to dodge — the one you count is Sky Splitter's 16 seconds. Farm to your spike.

edits.before: This is where it flips. W's bonus armor and empowered autos plus E's attack-speed slow start eating his auto-bite brawl, and Granite Shield lets you farm through his Q-in. At 6 your R is the equalizer — Unstoppable Force is unstoppable, so it goes through his E stun and W slow; bait his all-in, then R him up mid-commit and W-E him down while his attack speed is gutted. From here you out-armor a champion whose damage is mostly physical autos.
edits.after: This is where it flips. Thunderclap's bonus armor and Ground Slam's attack-speed slow start eating his brawl, and Granite Shield lets you farm through the Thundering Smash step-in. At 6 your R is the equalizer — bait the all-in, then knock him up mid-commit and W-E him while his attack speed is gutted. Sky Splitter is 16 seconds flat: once he throws it for the shield, you have the longest safe window in the lane to walk up and take a full trade.

edits.before: You're the favoured frontline now — your armor stacking and E attack-speed slow hard-counter his auto-heavy, AD brawl, so straight trades go your way. The danger is that Volibear is a diver and a scaler: his R disables a tower and shields him to dive your backline. Don't chase the 1v1 ego-kill on a fed Voli; instead hold R for the fight and use it to knock him up the instant he dives a carry. Turn the lane lead into teamfight tempo, not a sidelane duel.
edits.after: You're the favoured frontline now, but armor alone is not the whole answer: The Relentless Storm turns his stacked attack speed into bonus magic damage, so Ground Slam's attack-speed slow is the button that actually cuts it. The danger is the dive — Stormbringer disables a tower and pads his health. Don't chase the 1v1 ego-kill on a fed Voli; hold R and knock him up the instant he commits on a carry. Your ult is back 30 seconds before his.

edits.after: Thundering Smash closes and stuns, and Frenzied Maul heals him, before Thunderclap or Ground Slam exist — eat the poke and farm.
